content: Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget: a status event published while no WebSocket client is subscribed (task runs before UI connects, or client reconnects mid-run) is simply gone forever - the client that connects late never sees earlier transitions unless the current/full status is separately fetchable via REST. Redis Streams (not pub/sub) persist entries with monotonic IDs and support replay via XRANGE from a last-seen offset, enabling reconnect-and-catch-up; pub/sub alone cannot. Fast-publishing worker + slow WebSocket consumer risks unbounded growth of the per-connection outbound send buffer, which can exhaust memory if not bounded/monitored. For multi-worker API deployments, in-memory broadcast sets don't work across processes; must fan out via Redis so all API replicas' WebSocket connections see the same events.
